1.45.betting_forecast: 11/4 Rock Steady Beat, 7/2 Sir Sirius, 5/1 Statten Island, 6/1 The Ginger Kid, 9/1 Clash Of Hearts, Persian Spring, 10/1 Sue's Last
1.45.spotlight_verdict: Persian Spring should build on his recent Newmarket debut, while Rlasthope brings fair form to the table, but there is a feeling this may go to a newcomer. Before any betting clues are known ROCK STEADY BEAT, whose powerful stable won this with a newcomer in 2024, is preferred to Kevin Ryan pair Sir Sirius (second choice) and Statten Island. [Andrew Sheret]

horses.spotlight_comment: Early March foal by Mehmas; 120,000gns yearling; half-brother to yard's smart 2024 juvenile Symbol Of Strength (won Group 3 Sirenia and third in Gimcrack; later successful in Hong Kong); would enter calculations if the betting vibes are strong.
No better than mid-division in two outings over 5f at Beverley; needs to find significant improvement for this extra furlong.

Early May foal by Cotai Glory; 62,000gns yearling half-brother to winners Galileo Dame (1m2f Flat, RPR 97; 2m hurdle) and Mauna Queen (Norwegian 7f/1m4f); dam 9.4f winner (78); not necessarily bred to be an early type for yard also responsible for Clash Of Hearts.
Early February foal by Minzaal; 70,000euros yearling who is closely related to 6f 2yo winner French Affair (RPR 78); stable isn't really associated with first-time-out 2yo success.
Late April foal by Persian Force; shaped with some encouragement when 5l fifth of seven on his 5f debut at the recent Newmarket Guineas meeting; should improve for last year's winning stable.
Early April foal by Zoustar; Irish yard has sent out a 2yo winner in Britain this season but this colt offered only minor promise on his 5f Dundalk debut five weeks ago.

Showed promise when fifth of 15 in the Brocklesby at Doncaster and duly improved when pushing recent Lily Agnes winner Adonius close at Musselburgh (also 5f, good to soft) a fortnight later, albeit he received 5lb from that Rebecca Menzies-trained gelding; likely to stay 6f.

March foal by Minzaal; 110,000gns yearling; half-brother to five winners, notably Happy Romance (5f/6f including 2yo/Group 3; RPR 112); makes obvious paper appeal for a leading stable which won this with a newcomer in 2024.
Early February foal; 13,000gns yearling; Saxon Warrior filly out of a 1m2f winner (RPR 71); The Resdev Roman is the more obvious of the yard's pair on paper.

Fairly late February foal; 350,000gns yearling by Starman; half-brother to four winners, including Mehmento (7f including AW/Listed; RPR 109) and Immortal Beauty (6f turf/7f AW 2yo; 91); stable's 2yos going well, including a couple of promising first-time-out scorers; market confidence would look significant; yard also runs Statten Island.
January foal by Sioux Nation; £85,000 yearling; second foal of a mare who was placed over 10.5f/1m4f in France (RPR 73); best watched on his debut unless the betting hints otherwise.

65,000euros fairly early March foal; 180,000gns yearling by Starspangledbanner; half-brother to three winners, notably Raaeb (5f-7f including 2yo/AW/UAE dirt; RPR 108); one of two interesting debutants from the Kevin Ryan yard and the betting should help to separate them.

62,000euros early February foal; 125,000euros yearling by Cotai Glory; brother to 5f AW 2yo winner Elliott (RPR 62); dam US Listed-placed 1m/8.5f winner (90); stable yet to get off the mark with 2yos in 2026.

Late March foal by Mehmas; 110,000euros yearling; third foal out of an unraced half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 1 (Cheveley Park) winner Tiggy Wiggy; trainer had a first-time-out 2yo winner at Nottingham on Saturday; would enter calculations if the market vibes are strong.

Early March foal who cost £23,000 at last month's Doncaster breeze-up sale; half-sister to winners American Hope (French/German 7.5f/1m including AW; RPR 93), Tryst (8.6f AW 2yo; 86) and Vino Bello (French 1m-1m1f including 2yo/AW; 73); bred to have a future but will need to be very useful to take this first time out.

20,000euros late March foal; 16,000euros yearling; gelded son of Kodiac who is a brother to 5f AW winner Alhather (RPR 77) and half-brother to 5f winner Billie Be Quick (including 2yo; 93); yard wouldn't really be known for debut success in races like this but did have a ready 2yo winner at Beverley on Tuesday (second time out).

2.20.betting_forecast: 9/2 Corolla Point, 6/1 Air Force One, 8/1 Hammer The Hammer, 9/1 Redorange, 11/1 Arklow Lad, 12/1 Jakajaro, Ziggy's Triton,
2.20.spotlight_verdict: The drop back to 5f could be ideal for topweight HAMMER THE HAMMER and he is taken to make a winning reappearance. The very lightly raced 4yo Corolla Point could still have more to offer and is second choice ahead of last year's third Toca Madera, to whom new trainer David O'Meara may well find the key sooner rather than later. C&D winners Air Force One and Brazen Bolt could also be involved, along with the progressive Arklow Lad.[Ben Hutton]

horses.spotlight_comment: Third of 22 in 3yo handicap over C&D (good to firm) at this meeting 12 months ago and progressive on AW since; soft ground may not have suited at Musselburgh last time and he's had wind surgery since; however, a career best is needed today and he has to prove he's just as good on turf as AW.

Beat 18 rivals to win over C&D (good) last July and went close over 5.4f here on his next two starts; regained the winning thread at Beverley (5f, good to soft) four weeks ago and he's only 2lb higher today; respected.

Lightly raced 4yo who won on stable debut at Chelmsford (5f, AW) in February before good third at Wolverhampton (6f, AW), and he was back on the scoresheet in first-time cheekpieces (retained) at Pontefract (5f, good to soft) last month; could continue to progress for his new connections; chance.

8yo who was inconsistent last season and lacks a recent run; however, he's just 1lb higher than when both second of 13 over C&D (good) last May and winning at Hamilton (5f, good to soft) next time; not ruled out each-way.
horses.breeding: b g Kodi Bear - Fancy Vivid

horses.spotlight_comment: Won two 5f AW handicaps early last year and good fourth of 16 in the 3yo Dash at Epsom (5f, good) last June, when 3lb higher; however, he's 0-11 since his last win and others arrive with more pressing claims.
horses.breeding: ch g Mehmas - Goodnight And Joy

horses.spotlight_comment: Won big-field handicaps over C&D (good to firm) and at Goodwood (5f, good) last July, and this 9yo returned from wind surgery with a back-to-form, neck second at Thirsk (5f, good to firm) 12 days ago; Harry Vigors removes a valuable 7lb and this prominent-racer could be bang there once more.
horses.breeding: b g Brazen Beau - Gladys' Gal

horses.spotlight_comment: Hugely admirable 12yo whose seven York wins include this race in 2019 and 2021, and he built upon last month's reappearance second at Ripon (5f, good) to win at Beverley (5f, good to soft) ten days ago; however, there's a suspicion he may find a big-field Class 2 such as this too hot nowadays.
horses.breeding: b g Sir Prancealot - Mystic Dream

horses.spotlight_comment: Very lightly raced, ex-Godolphin 4yo; won on stable debut at Haydock (5f, good) last September and followed up later that month (5f, soft); reappeared with close third to Air Force One at Beverley (5f, good to soft) four weeks ago and this unexposed sort could still have plenty more to offer.
horses.breeding: b g Blue Point - Platinum Coast

horses.spotlight_comment: Trainer won this last year with subsequent Group 1 winner American Affair; progressive last season and she's 1lb lower than when a close third of 18 over C&D (good) last October; however, well beaten on both starts this season (irregular heartbeat last time) and a major turnaround is needed.

Second of 24 in the 5f 3yo handicap at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm) last June and he showed good speed before fading into sixth of 19 over 6f here (good) last October, when last seen; wind op since; the drop back in trip could be a positive move on his reappearance; can make a bold bid.

5yo who raced over further until this year, and her three career-best RPRs have come on her three attempts at 5f; kept on well for close fourth of 14 at Musselburgh (5f, soft) last month on a rare outing on turf, and she's an each-way contender if handling the forecast better ground.

He's been an improved model this year and won a shade cosily at Beverley (5f, good) last month; his subsequent run at Musselburgh (5f, good) three days later, when fourth, may have come too soon and further progress can't be ruled out, but it's necessary with this step up in grade.

Snapped a lengthy losing sequence when making virtually all to win at Newmarket (5f, good) last month on his reappearance; he needs to back up that performance but did it comfortably last time and, following a 5lb rise, remains well treated on his historic exploits; a possible.
horses.breeding: b g Too Darn Hot - Summer Flower

horses.spotlight_comment: Two wins last autumn and he's better than he's shown at Pontefract and Ascot of late; however, this is tougher and he needs to raise his game.
horses.breeding: b g Lethal Force - Little Nymph

horses.spotlight_comment: Front-runner who was a highly progressive 3yo last season, making it six wins for the campaign when scoring here (5.4f, good) last July; very close third of 19 over this C&D (good to firm) next time; suited by this course and could give a good account on her reappearance.

Won off this mark in small field at Southwell (5f, AW) in March; ran pretty well on next two starts but down the field at Thirsk (5f, good to firm) latest and others are preferred in a hotter race than he's used to.
horses.breeding: b g Bungle Inthejungle - Jackie Sparrow

horses.spotlight_comment: Won off 7lb higher over C&D (good) last June and he's one to watch in the betting; an underwhelming autumn was followed by a fairly encouraging reappearance run at Beverley last month, but he was down the field at Thirsk last time and is back to having something to prove.

Won the big-field 3yo Dash at Epsom (5f, good) last June and landed another quality handicap at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) in July; she lacks a recent run and there is a suspicion that 6f is her optimum trip, but she'll get a strong pace to aim at today and is not ruled out off a competitive mark.
horses.breeding: b f Study Of Man - Colorada

horses.spotlight_comment: Did well for new yard last autumn, winning three times (5f, AW/good to soft), and he returned to form when second of six at Bath (5f, good) recently; however, he may prove vulnerable in this hotter contest.
horses.breeding: gr g Invincible Army - Angelic Light

horses.spotlight_comment: His form has gone the wrong way since he was third in this last year (good to firm), behind two subsequent Group-race winners, and he needs a good step forward from his recent stable/seasonal debut at Thirsk (5f, good to firm) where he was seventh; however, he's 8lb lower than 12 months ago and could be just the type that David O'Meara excels with; interesting contender.
horses.breeding: b g Bated Breath - Hala Hala

horses.spotlight_comment: Back on better ground when he returned to form with a win at Musselburgh (5f, good) last month, taking his strike-rate to 5-22; did well to come out of top from a wide draw and this 4yo could go well up 5lb.

2.55.betting_forecast: 3/1 Sea Force, 11/2 Shout, 13/2 Cerulean Bay, 9/1 Mirsky, 11/1 Maybe Not, Walsingham, 12/1 Point Of Contact, 14/1 Diego
2.55.spotlight_verdict: Topweight POINT LYNAS has a very solid record at York, including an all-the-way win in this race in 2024, and he can capitalise on stall 1. Sea Force may well have won the Thirsk Hunt Cup granted a clear passage and he is feared most. The improving Walsingham is next on the list, while stablemates Cerulean Bay and Mirsky could also be in the mix. Point Of Contact and Maybe Not are 4yos who might have more to offer.[Ben Hutton]

horses.spotlight_comment: Progressive last term, winning two in a row at Goodwood (1m, good to soft/good) in the autumn, and kept on well for a close fourth on last month's reappearance at Haydock (7f, good to firm); solid claims back up to 1m.
horses.breeding: b g New Bay - Kathy Sun

horses.spotlight_comment: Ray Dawson 66-1 95 93 - Won this for the Crisfords in 2023 when 1lb higher; missed all of 2024 and 2025 and down the field at 40-1 on last month's stable debut at Haydock; he may have needed that run but has to prove how much ability he retains.

7f Listed winner at Longchamp last May and he ran some good races subsequently in Group/Listed contests; below par on last month's reappearance at Longchamp but may have needed the run; could go well in first handicap.
Two 1m wins on turf last season and added another on AW at Lingfield (1m2f) in December; however, he needs to produce a bigger performance than he's managed across his four outings this year.

Well handicapped on last year's best form (including on turf) and ran okay when third of six at Southwell (1m, AW) last month; however, he's been hard to win with on grass and looks vulnerable back up in grade.
horses.breeding: b g Cotai Glory - Dream Impossible

horses.spotlight_comment: Having been gelded last autumn he enjoyed a good stint on AW, winning twice (1m/8.6f); soundly beaten at Newcastle (1m, AW) last time and he needs to transfer his improvement back to turf, but he remains lightly raced for his top yard and is not discounted under Ryan Moore.

On a competitive mark on last year's best efforts but he's without a win since September 2022 and finished merely in mid-division on reappearance in the Lincoln at Doncaster in March (unseated rider on the way to post).

Won the Lincoln at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) last March and followed up at Newcastle (1m, AW); of interest on those efforts but he went off the boil on his final three starts for William Haggas; needs to get back on track on stable debut (remains in same ownership); slow ground would aid cause.

Three wins last June-September (7f-1m) along with 1l second of 18 in a fillies' handicap here (7f, good to firm), and she's better than she showed at Newmarket (1m, good) on her final outing last season; this lightly raced 4yo is in excellent hands to continue to progress and she's one to consider.

7yo who has returned in top form this term, finishing third at Musselburgh (1m1f, good) then winning the Thirsk Hunt Cup (1m, good to firm) 12 days ago; effective over C&D; could be bang there once more up 3lb for last time.

Won this off 1lb lower last year (good to firm); however, soundly beaten over C&D (good to firm) last August on final run for Ed Bethell and down the field on last month's stable/seasonal debut at Newbury (1m, good).

Below best on final two starts last season and same story on sole run this term, in Qatar in February; also has a hefty mark to defy but this front-runner was a fine second under an enterprising ride in a Group 2 at Ascot last July and has a strong record here, finishing second in this race in 2023 and winning it in 2024; capable of very bold bid from the inside stall.

Respectable efforts last July-September after moving into handicaps, the best run coming over C&D (good to firm) in August when close fifth of 17; gelded since last seen and it's possible this lightly raced 4yo will have more to offer for his good yard this term.

Won at Yarmouth (1m1f, soft) last September on final 3yo start and returned to form when third to Mirsky in the Thirsk Hunt Cup (1m, good to firm) 12 days ago in reapplied cheekpieces (retained), which he may well have won granted a clear run; lightly raced and in top hands; firmly in calculations.
horses.breeding: b g Sea The Stars - Pretty Baby

horses.spotlight_comment: Progressive 3yo last season (on various ground), winning a big-field 1m handicap at Ascot in September; reappeared with encouraging run in the Lincoln at Doncaster and he's not written off, but he was somewhat underwhelming in the Spring Cup at Newbury last time when favourite.

Second of 14 off 1lb higher behind Thunder Roar at Ayr (1m) last September on his favoured soft ground, and didn't run badly when 4l 11th of 21 in the Lincoln at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) on his reappearance; however, others have more compelling credentials.
7yo who was better than ever last season, a campaign that concluded with a fine second of 17 over C&D (good); races off the same mark today but he hasn't shone on his two outings this year.
horses.breeding: ch g Night Of Thunder - Dominike

horses.spotlight_comment: 8yo who is without a win since December 2023 but he showed spark in Dubai this winter and ran big races on his two previous visits to York; returns to a handy on a fair mark and could have an each-way shout.

Ran just four times last year, winning on three occasions (1m, good/soft), and back on the scoresheet at Pontefract (1m, good) a fortnight ago on his second start of the season; did it cosily last time and a 4lb rise may not stop this thriving 6yo.
horses.breeding: b g Lope De Vega - Dark Crusader

3.30.betting_forecast: 6/5 See The Fire, 11/4 Fallen Angel, 3/1 Diamond Rain, 7/1 Red Letter.
3.30.spotlight_verdict: Five Group 1 wins make Fallen Angel the class act of this field but she wasn't at her best on her reappearance in 2024 or 2025. Dancing Rain developed into a very smart performer last year but her stable has found winners hard to come by in recent weeks so this might be best left to SEE THE FIRE again. Jeff Smith's mare wasn't close to her best when just lasting home in a Nottingham Listed race 18 days ago but that's presumably because she wasn't fully primed for that first run of the season and her high-class performance in this race last year came with an outing her belt. [Andrew Sheret]

horses.spotlight_comment: An improved performer last year, winning a good-ground Listed race at Haydock (reappearance) and AW Group 3 at Newcastle around 1m2f before progressing again to place in Grade 1s on firm at Woodbine (1m2f) and Del Mar (1m3f; Breeders' Cup Filly & Mare Turf); bang there on form but the fact her top stable has gone nearly three weeks without a winner has to be a slight concern.

Gained a breakthrough Listed success at Lingfield (1m5f, AW) on her final 4yo start and added Group 2 wins over 1m1f and 2m at Meydan (both good) in February/March; versatile and talented but will need another career best back in Britain.

Won three 1m Group 1s against her own sex last year, namely the Prix Rothschild, Matron and Sun Chariot (all good/good to yielding); tackles 1m2f for just the second time on her seasonal return (wasn't strong at the finish when fourth in the 2024 Prix de l'Opera on previous attempt but it was only just short of her best RPR at the time); has to carry a 3lb penalty and wasn't at her best on her reappearance in 2024 or 2025; top mare but there are reasons to oppose her this time.
horses.breeding: gr m Too Darn Hot - Agnes Stewart

horses.spotlight_comment: Winner of a Listed race at Killarney (1m, soft) and Group 3 at the Curragh (1m1f, good to yielding) last summer; creditable third of 12 in 1m2f Group 3 back at the Curragh (soft) on reappearance 25 days ago; likely to give a good account but has a bit to find on ratings.

4.05.betting_forecast: 2/1 Christmas Day, 7/2 Morshdi, 6/1 Action, Item, 8/1 King's Trail, 11/1 Wise Prince, 14/1 Al Zanati, 20/1 Guildmaster.
4.05.spotlight_verdict: All have Derby entries except for Al Zanati, who was not in it even before the Sandown Classic Trial, and Wise Prince who was withdrawn after it. Both of them beat Action in that Group 3, with the O'Brien runner not looking on his game at all but he tops the ratings on the strength of his close second in the Group 1 Futurity last October. That came in the mud and was comfortably his most persuasive display, so he may need rain, and CHRISTMAS DAY is the stable first string anyway, judged on jockey bookings. Ryan Moore's mount has been progressing well and his Ballysax win earns him narrow preference over Morshdi who won with some authority in the Listed Feilden Stakes at Newmarket. Item is unexposed but very promising after winning two minor races as a 2yo.[Richard Austen]

horses.spotlight_comment: Closely related to 2025 Derby winner Lambourn; carries head high but progressed with every start last season and ended it with a close, battling second to one of his stablemates in the Group 1 Futurity at Doncaster (1m, heavy); consequently 4-6 for Group 3 Classic Trial at Sandown (1m2f, good) three weeks ago but sluggish leaving the stalls and for most of the race before mustering something to finish fourth of seven; perhaps a first-time tongue-tie that day backfired, and he now goes without; the form pick if he bounces back.

Won debut last August and a 1m1f AW Group 3 at Chantilly in November; runner-up in British Group 3s in his other two starts, on reappearance starting 11-2 for Group 3 Classic Trial at Sandown (1m2f, good; unraced on softer) and keeping on steadily from rear to be second of seven, with Wise Prince and Action the next two behind him; that's not the best form in this field but he could still bring potential.

Won a heavy-ground maiden on third 2yo start and led on the post in Group 3 at Leopardstown (1m1f, yielding) in October; 11-1 with three of his stablemates among those at shorter odds when he reappeared in nine-runner Group 3 Ballysax at Leopardstown (1m2f, good to yielding) last month but it was him who asserted in the final 1f to win by half a length; will stay further but looks firmly in the mix.

Favourite for novice at Lingfield (1m, AW) in December and eventually got on top despite looking green; perhaps didn't make as much improvement as expected when third of five almost throughout in novice at Newmarket (1m2f, good; 100-30) four weeks ago, which leaves him requiring a big step forward in this contest but that track may not have suited; early days still.

Well on top last September in a maiden at Kempton (7f, AW) and four-runner novice at Bath (1m, good to firm); non-runner in Group 1 Futurity in October due to heavy going; this Frankel colt has a lot to find on ratings but he's a fascinating prospect who looks sure to be suited by 1m2f+.

Left good impression with 1m wins on Kempton AW in December and March, the latter in a good conditions stakes; just 13-2 for the 2,000 Guineas at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) 12 days ago and he was bang there 3f out to 2f out, but floundered thereafter and finished ninth of 14; likely to stay 1m2f but needs to prove that his run in that recent Classic was all wrong.
horses.breeding: ch c Sea The Stars - Crown Walk

horses.spotlight_comment: Brother to 1m2f and 14.5f (Group 2) winner Nakheel (RPR 110); won here (1m, good) on second start as 2yo and followed up in clearcut style in seven-runner Listed race at Newmarket (1m1f, good) four weeks ago; non-runner in 1m2f Listed race at Chester last week given the problem they had with the track; he has one of the best chances on form in this field and is on his way up.
horses.breeding: ch c Dubawi - Into The Mystic

horses.spotlight_comment: Scored comfortably in six-runner novice at Nottingham (1m, good to soft) in October on his only start as 2yo; 6-1 for Group 3 Classic Trial at Sandown (1m2f, good) on return three weeks ago and kept on to split Al Zanati and Action in third of seven, having raced freely early on; major work to do and something to learn, but he could still be a good prospect.

4.40.betting_forecast: 11/4 Aspect Island, 3/1 Manatee Mehmas, Revival Power, 7/1 Simplify, 9/1 Dickensian, 12/1 Black Star Boy, 20/1 Exclamation,
4.40.spotlight_verdict: Aspect Island (second choice) commands maximum respect on any of his last three efforts, while Manatee Mehmas made a striking debut 19 days ago and is a fascinating prospect up sharply in grade. However, it's tempting to side with C&D winner REVIVAL POWER (nap), who is treading a similar path to her Nunthorpe-winning sister and can defy a Group 2 penalty on this return. Dickensian holds solid each-way claims and Wor Faayth may also reward similar support.[Richard Russell]

horses.spotlight_comment: Won Yarmouth nursery (6f, soft) in September but better form when third in Group 3 Cornwallis at Newmarket (good) and Grade 1 Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf Sprint (again 5f, firm) the following month; looked to have trained on when beaten around 2l in all-aged Group 3 at Newmarket four weeks ago; holds Group 1 entries over 5f and 6f at Royal Ascot and now drops back into his own age group; sets the standard.

Newbury maiden (good to soft) winner who was gelded after finishing down the field in Listed event here (also 6f) in October; coped well with the drop to 5f when taking good step forward to land Sandown handicap (good) on his reappearance three weeks ago; unexposed and likely capable of better again.

Sole success came in four-runner Hamilton maiden (5f, good to soft) but it was a fine effort when second at 66-1 in very valuable sales at the Ebor meeting (6f, good to firm) and bettered that form when runner-up in Listed race back here (good) in October; floundered on heavy ground next time, however, and down the field in Newmarket handicap on return; work to do even if this track brings out the best in him again.

All starts at 5f on good or good to firm; no wins since his debut success at Musselburgh 13 months ago but he ran a belter when second of 20 in the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot; again very useful form when beaten around 2l by Revival Power in Listed C&D event in August and Doncaster Group 2 three weeks later; solid each-way claims on this reappearance.

Raced mainly at 5f; won Doncaster novice (good to soft) last summer and bettered that form when fifth to Revival Power in Doncaster Group 2 (80-1) in September; doubled his tally when producing career best to make all in Chester handicap (good) on Friday; drawn on the wing but could be the sort to run above himself.

105,000gns yearling whose dam is closely related to 6f Group 2 winner Tasleet; sent off odds-on for his debut in Doncaster novice (5f, good to firm) where he made stylish headway before dispatching his main market rival with ease 19 days ago; goes straight into Listed company and he's a fascinating contender.

0-11 but she went close when beaten a neck in Newbury Listed race in August; similar form when seventh to Revival Power in Doncaster Group 2 in September and when sixth of 14 in Bath Listed event (also 5f, good) on last month's return; likely to find a few too good again.
horses.breeding: ch f Havana Grey - Miss Villanelle

horses.spotlight_comment: Progressed well last year, making all in Listed event over C&D (good to firm) at the Ebor meeting in August and Doncaster's Group 2 Flying Childers (5f, good) three weeks later; holds a Group 1 entry at Royal Ascot and her sister Winter Power, also a Group-race winning juvenile, won this race in 2021 before landing the Nunthorpe later that year; carries a penalty on this return but a bold bid looks likely.
horses.breeding: ch f Bungle Inthejungle - Titian Saga

horses.spotlight_comment: Improving filly who made all in Thirsk novice (6f, good) on her final start of last term and carried on the good work when making a winning seasonal/handicap debut at Wolverhampton (5f, AW) in March; completed the hat-trick with best effort yet in Thirsk handicap (5f, good) last month and she's not discounted in her bid for the four-timer representing last year's winning yard.

Won Beverley maiden (soft; debut) and Chester nursery (good to soft) last term; again scored on first start of the year when taking AW handicap (also 5f) in March; possibly found 6f a stretch again when disappointing at Chester last Wednesday but this looks too warm even if she does get back to her best.
horses.breeding: b f Magna Grecia - Dance Hall Girl

horses.spotlight_comment: Made all in Hamilton maiden (5f, good) in June and won French Listed race (6f, good) on her next start in July; little went right in the Group 2 Lowther here (good to firm) the following month and wasn't disgraced in Chantilly Group 3 (6f, good to soft) when last seen in September; unexposed at this trip and she's not without interest ahead of her comeback.

5.15.betting_forecast: 7/2 Arc Ole Ole, 11/2 Hard To Believe, 7/1 Baltic Fleet, 8/1 Charles Darnay, 9/1 Sudbury Hill, 10/1 Cotton Bud, Heroics, 11/1
5.15.spotlight_verdict: The 1m2f handicap win for ARC OLE OLE at Doncaster in March came by just a short head but that's led to a modest rise in the weights and Dylan Cunha's charge clearly retains significant potential. He is selected to win for the third time in a row, even though today's warm field also includes some notable handicap newcomers who may be headed by Knightsail (second choice), Northern Brave, Charles Darnay and Baltic Fleet.[Richard Austen]

horses.spotlight_comment: Scored comfortably at Bath (1m, soft) last October on second start and narrowly got the better of a serious battle for eight-runner handicap at Doncaster (1m2f, good to soft) in March on reappearance; raised 4lb but that latest start is solid form and this scopey, long-striding sort, who's well related, looks set for further improvement, including at 1m4f.
horses.breeding: b c Study Of Man - Alma Linda

horses.spotlight_comment: Short-head winner of a Yarmouth maiden (1m1f, good to soft) in September on second start; couldn't get near the winner in a novice at Bath (1m2f, good) on reappearance but made late gains, suggesting this trip will help on handicap debut; also gelded the day after; needs a second look.
horses.breeding: ch g Space Blues - Duchess Of Danzig

horses.spotlight_comment: Made his debut in January and all three starts have been on AW; upped from 1m to 1m4f when 11-10 favourite for nine-runner maiden at Kempton ten weeks ago on latest start, responding well to sustained pressure to get up in the final strides; while this handicap/turf debut demands more, he should retain potential for 1m4f+.

Steady progress in four starts for Kevin Philippart De Foy as 2yo, before sold for £26,000gns; 11-1 for nine-runner handicap at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) three weeks ago and came from last to first to get off the mark at first time of asking for new connections; up 5lb but 1m4f should be within reach and she probably has more to give.
horses.breeding: b f Cloth Of Stars - Pink Anemone

horses.spotlight_comment: Eight-race maiden, with new yard this season; upped to 1m2f, hooded and came from the rear on last two outings when close third to Arc Ole Ole at Doncaster (good to soft) and second of eight at Nottingham (good); shapes as if he'll get 1m4f, despite speedy family.
horses.breeding: b g New Bay - Jo Jo Air

horses.spotlight_comment: Made a low-key debut on heavy ground last September but landed a gamble at Bath (1m, good to soft) the following month and made all when odds-on again in a five-runner novice at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) in March; the latter performance was on the workmanlike side but gave plenty of encouragement for this longer trip on handicap debut.
horses.breeding: b g Make Believe - Heat Of The Day

horses.spotlight_comment: Had four races as 2yo, showing easily best form when triple-figure odds over 1m at Pontefract (good to soft) and York (good) on last two starts; straight up to 1m4f (dam 1m4f winner) for this handicap/seasonal debut under 7lb claimer and he's one to keep an eye on.
horses.breeding: b g Bated Breath - Bella Varenna

horses.spotlight_comment: Often front-runner; 3-4 in handicaps last term; back with two creditable supporting roles in five-runner handicaps at Kempton (1m3f, AW) when it looked like he would be suited by 1m4f+, but he failed to prove that when never dangerous and well beaten at Chester (good) last week with cheekpieces first enlisted; others are preferred.
horses.breeding: b g Study Of Man - Suffused

horses.spotlight_comment: 33-1 winner in a novice at Thirsk (7f, soft) last September, coming from towards rear; improved form stepping up in trip when third in his two handicaps since, latest when 25-1 in seven-runner race over 1m4f at Doncaster (good to firm) on reappearance; may be able to build on that.

Best efforts to take minor honours in handicaps for new stable on all three starts this season, over 1m2f on last two occasions; lost out in a sustained duel at Redcar (good to firm) last time but kept on well; not the most stoutly bred and today's extra distance needs to spark some improvement.
horses.breeding: b g Cotai Glory - La Cuvee

horses.spotlight_comment: Second or third in four of his five starts, all this year; latest was his turf and handicap debut at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) three weeks ago when third of nine to Cotton Bud; not bred for this far.

Tailed off in two turf races on good last July; firmly on the up in AW handicaps when last seen, registering a quickfire hat-trick in February and last two starts were at 1m4f (made all last time); absent since and this is a much more competitive contest for his return to turf.
horses.breeding: b g Expert Eye - Dusty Red
